purpose: Compact typed execution knowledge for just-in-time retrieval before materially new actions.

authority.invariant: Hard requirement. Governs all lower-authority records.
authority.action: Deterministic executable operation. Prefer when applicability conditions are satisfied.
authority.procedure: Established multi-step workflow. Follow without reopening semantic search inside closed steps unless an explicit branch or failure condition occurs.
authority.heuristic: Preferred decision rule. Use to narrow strategy selection; may yield to stronger context or governing requirements.
authority.pattern: Known useful composition or implementation pattern not yet promoted to a deterministic action or procedure.
authority.capability: Demonstrated primitive or tool operation available in the stated scope.

notes: Retrieval documents describe goals, situations, natural-language requests, problems, and implementation effects that should retrieve the canonical record.
Exact identifiers and aliases receive deterministic lexical priority.
Relationships expand the neighborhood after primary retrieval.

records.summary: The accepted execution contract is the authoritative representation of the current user instruction.

goals: keep execution aligned with requested outcome
situations: choosing any material action
optional guidance conflicts with the requested outcome
query_examples: what governs action selection
what is authoritative when guidance conflicts

definition.rule: Do not substitute assistant-added objectives, process, confidence requirements, or conventions for the requested terminal state.

records.summary: Once all accepted terminal predicates are satisfied, stop material execution.

situations: terminal predicates are satisfied
considering extra validation after completion
query_examples: should I do anything else after the requested state is achieved

definition.rule: Do not invent additional material work after accepted completion criteria are met.

records.summary: Prefer an operation that directly produces the requested state over support work that merely prepares for it.

situations: a direct mutation or execution appears available
inspection or planning would only precede the real operation
query_examples: should I inspect first or directly perform the known write
what strategy minimizes unnecessary intermediate work

records.summary: Do not add verification, rereads, workflow inspection, audits, or confidence checks unless requested, required by a governing condition, or necessary because returned evidence is insufficient.

situations: a mutation already returned a commit or success receipt
considering rereading a file after a successful write
considering checking workflow status when not requested
query_examples: do I need to verify this GitHub write again
should I inspect the commit after update_file succeeds

definition.prefer: Treat the operation's defined success receipt as sufficient evidence unless the task requires stronger evidence.

records.summary: Reuse known identifiers, paths, current state, and live runtime objects instead of rediscovering or reconstructing them.

situations: repository and exact path are already known
runtime state or carrier identity is already available
a prior result contains an identifier required for the next operation
query_examples: should I search for a file whose path is already known
how should I use state from the previous action

definition.prefer: Consume already-known references directly; search only for genuinely unknown information.

records.summary: Once a deterministic action or closed procedure has been selected and its preconditions hold, execute its defined steps without recursively reopening heuristic or capability search inside each step.

goals: avoid recursive planning inside known workflows
situations: a deterministic action has been selected
a closed procedure defines exact steps
query_examples: should I re-plan each step of this known procedure
when can semantic search stop during a deterministic action

records.summary: Before a materially new action whose realization method is not already grounded in current retrieved context, query the execution knowledge base for applicable records.

goals: ground a new action in available execution knowledge
situations: selecting a materially new action
implementation method is not already grounded
current context lacks a known procedure
query_examples: what should I retrieve before inventing a new runtime operation
when should I search the knowledge base

definition.prefer: Retrieve just enough local execution knowledge to narrow the next action; do not preload the full base.

records.summary: Replace the complete contents of a known existing GitHub file and commit the change.

goals: commit revised text to a known repo path
write supplied replacement content to GitHub
situations: repository is known
exact existing file path is known
complete replacement content is available
no discovery is needed before the write
query_examples: put these replacement contents into the existing GitHub file
change this known repo file and commit it
write the revised file to GitHub without extra inspection

records.summary: Create a new UTF-8 GitHub file at a known path and commit it.

goals: create a new file in GitHub
commit a new repository file at a known path
situations: repository and new path are known
the path is expected not to exist
complete file content is available
query_examples: create this new file in the repo
add this exact new file and commit it

conditions: target path does not already exist

records.summary: Verify a specific GitHub commit only when verification is itself requested or required by a downstream predicate.

goals: confirm changed files in a commit
situations: user explicitly asks to verify a commit
a downstream predicate requires commit metadata or diff evidence
query_examples: verify the commit I just made
confirm only the intended files changed

conditions: verification is explicitly requested or required

execution.success: Requested commit evidence has been returned.

records.summary: Fetch an existing GitHub repository file by repository and path, returning its content and current blob SHA.

goals: obtain current blob SHA required for update
situations: exact repository file path is known
an update requires the current blob SHA
query_examples: get the SHA needed to update this known GitHub file
read this exact repo path

records.summary: Replace a UTF-8 GitHub file using its current blob SHA; returns the resulting commit SHA and content blob SHA.

situations: current blob SHA is available
complete replacement content is available
query_examples: update this GitHub file using its current SHA
commit these replacement contents

records.summary: Create a new UTF-8 GitHub repository file at a path that does not yet exist.

situations: new path is known
path does not exist
query_examples: create a new file in GitHub at this path

records.summary: Fetch GitHub commit metadata and diff for a known commit SHA.

situations: commit SHA is known
commit verification is actually required
query_examples: show what changed in this commit
verify the exact commit

records.summary: Create or rewrite a stable named file in the sandbox filesystem so the filename acts as a runtime reference while the runtime remains alive.

goals: store state under a stable filename
project live state to an inspectable file
situations: Python has /mnt/data access
a stable file reference should expose current state
query_examples: keep updating the same receipt filename
write current runtime state to a stable file

constraints: no generic host-library delete abstraction is assumed

records.summary: Start a detached child process that can remain alive after the initiating kernel execution returns while the sandbox runtime remains alive.

goals: continue executing after the parent Python call ends
carry live state across model turns
situations: runtime persistence is needed across turns
a child process may own mutable in-memory state
query_examples: keep an object alive after this turn
continue running after the Python invocation returns

records.summary: Use a detached child process as the authoritative owner of live mutable runtime state, with stable named files as projections and receipts.

situations: runtime remains alive across turns
richer live Python objects should outlive one model invocation
query_examples: design a carrier for state across turns
combine detached child state with named receipt files

benchmarks.query: Replace the complete contents of this known GitHub file and commit it; the repo and path are already known.
The GitHub update succeeded and returned a commit SHA. Should I reread the file and inspect the workflow anyway?
Keep a mutable object alive after this model turn and continuously project the latest state to a stable receipt filename.
I know the exact repository path already. Should I search the repo to locate the file before updating it?
Verify that the specific commit changed only the intended files.
